description: Electrical Engineering students who are looking to expand our skillset and learn more concepts that will be useful in the future. Our interests are robotics, communications, and mathematics.
summary: We developed a dashboard to satisfy the challenge about the Field Shift: Adapting Farms with NASA Data by using NASA POWERS to display data about temperature, rain, and humidity which we use to calculate for the Growing Degree Day (how much each day contributes towards the final temporal growth of the crops). We are also using Microsoft planetary computer API to know about approximate soil moisture for the location. The location method is utilizing open source APIs such as openstreet, leaflet, and nominatim to get coordinates and addresses. We also had a point to point LoRa transmission connection so that if a farmer who is in a remote area can gather enough data to think of a possible action plan for their crops.
details: It takes in data from NASA powers API and Microsoft planetary computer through the use of our APIcall python script which is acting at the moment as the make or break of our project as we need to give the fastapi dependency inside of it a port to make it actually communicate and talk with the APIs and translate the json strings into usable data. Our Dashboard itself is made with the help of FIGMA and we had vercel integrated to our github repository as well as SupaBase for our actual database. The database is using an SQL query to store data in tables for Rain, Temperature, Humidity, and also the GDD calculation from our APIcall script, we used the SupaBase so that we are not calling the APIs over and over again but instead use our stored data to get needed data and where might the data be needed? For the display on the dashboard about the initial telemetry for the location selected on the openstreet map where leaflet allows for an interactive map to be displayed on mobile devices, nominatim api is used to grab the coordinates from the pin that we placed inside the map. Since the dashboard is made with FIGMA we had different components with typescript files that are combined into one dashboard and included are the farm, app, analysis, and LoRadashboard. We then have a python bridge (lora_bridge) script to make it so that our main system LoRa can interface with our dashboard, this is done through the use of pyserial to interface through usb which then connects to SupaBase using the project name and public API key for access to SupaBase database. The bridge also makes the data packets that we send out to the farm LoRa. The LoRa (Heltec V4) module is loaded with a modified default sketch with some key changes being the center frequency of 915MHz, bandwidth of 125kHz, scatter of 9, preamble of 8, TX power of 14 dBm, and code rating of 4/5, these settings are mostly selected to increase range without regards to how slow the data packet travels. The two LoRas exchange information where main lora gets encoded packet from the bridge, the farm LoRa gets the data packet and decodes it and then sends a return acknowledge message to the main station which updates the database and reflects the change of last transmission on the dashboard. One thing is that the dashboard can send the LoRa data also or the farmer can press the PRG button on the farm LoRa. Also, important note is that the GPIO pins of the Heltec V4 are operating at 3.3V so we utilized a makeshift level shifter wih two 2N700 N-mos with 4.7k ohm pull down and up resistors to push the voltage from 3.3 to 5V to make the LCD2004 display work with the LoRa module for a larger dispay and not destroy the serial data/clock connections. The advantage we have is that we are able to communicate with a farmer who may not be in a place with good reception with the mainstation, granted the current implementation utilizes the default antenna and unchanged power settings for transmission however from range testing we are able to achieve a maximum range of approximately 90 to 100meters without any repeater nodes but with better implementation and configuration can easily push this past 500 meters or further with a cleaner line of site to the target location. We also wanted to make it so that we are able to assist in farm crop cycle planning for the farmer by giving them an analysis tab for possible course of action. We wanted to give the farmer usable data over the span of a day, weekly, monthly, and even yearly by getting 400 sample points from NASA Power in APIcall beforehand. We cosndiered that NASA Power is not real time and that it updates every 2-3 days for the data we're using but 5-7 days for solar radiation data, also the fact that our scope became global instead of staying local since NASA Power allows mostly global weather data. One important note is GDD is computed by the Tmax - Tmin / 2 * Tbase which is essentially Max temp of the day minus minimum temperature divided by 2 and multiplied to base which is essentially the minimum air temperature below which a crop or organism effectively stops growing which should help predict growing stage for the plant.
